title: Old brass bands, Walter Blue and other trumpeters
summary: Bands then were incomparable to today's; Walter Blue died playing a parade and other trumpet players are named.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: They just played, they played though. When you heard those bands coming down the street talking about Eureka, and these little bands, little bands you hear today, I'm not panning them to be good these days. But, I mean, you couldn't do no comparison. Oh no, man, no comparison. No comparison, man. You all don't hear the real thing. It's too bad. Couldn't catch those people on tape. No. Catch them trumpet players, liking people. Butter Petit. Walter Blue, huh?
Walter Blue, oh. He was a good trumpet player.
He died on the street. Yeah, he died on the street. He died playing the parade.
Yeah, he fell asleep. Who ought to talk to his son?
Walter Blue, he was good. His son played something.
Huh? His son plays millionaires. Oh yeah. He might remember something, Bill. Yeah. He was too small, but his mother could tell.
I had a man of trumpet players in those days. I mean, they had Chip, they had Joe Johnson, they had, let's see, come on trumpet players. Edwin Clemons, he was good. So many guys.
